title: extract /api/extract crashes with bare 502 when pipeline throws unhandled
description:
## Symptom

\`POST /api/extract\` returns HTTP 502 with NO error body — Vercel-gateway empty 502 = unhandled exception in the function. Same route returns 200 for other inputs, so it's input-dependent.

## Root cause

\`apps/web/src/routes/api/extract/+server.ts\` has zero try/catch around the three pipeline stages: \`safeFetch\`, \`extractContent\`, \`vardScanner.scan\`. An unhandled exception in any of them bubbles to SvelteKit's default error path → Vercel returns 502 with empty body. The most likely throwing path is Readability.parse() inside extractContent on pathological HTML (no try/catch at packages/agent/src/url/extract.ts:117). Other candidates: ipaddr.parse() on edge-case IPs in ssrf.ts:13, DNS lookup ENOTFOUND in ssrf.ts:40, vard detector init in sanitize.ts:44.

## Acceptance criteria

- Handler returns a structured 5xx response with a typed error kind (not bare 502 with empty body) when any pipeline stage throws.
- Server logs include the exception's class/name (e.g., 'TypeError', 'RangeError') so the actual root-cause is observable on the next reproduction without code changes.
- No exception is allowed to escape the handler. Defense-in-depth.
- Test exists that simulates an unhandled exception in the pipeline and asserts a structured response.

## Affected files

- apps/web/src/routes/api/extract/+server.ts (modify — wrap pipeline in try/catch)
- apps/web/tests/extract-route.test.ts (modify — add unhandled-exception test)

title: chat /api/chat returns AI_MissingToolResultsError on every turn after the first
description:
## Symptom

`POST /api/chat` returns HTTP 200 but the stream contains an error part. Server logs show `{ kind: 'streamText.error', name: 'AI_MissingToolResultsError' }`. First turn after page load always works; every subsequent turn fails. The frontend surfaces 'Upstream provider error' (the sanitised onError string).

## Root cause

`packages/agent/src/tools/finalize.ts` defines the \`finalize\` tool intentionally WITHOUT an \`execute\` function (client-side sentinel tool pattern). The model calls it to end the turn; the SDK never produces a tool-result. On the NEXT turn, \`packages/agent/src/agent.ts:119\` calls \`convertToModelMessages(messages)\` and walks the history. It sees an assistant message with a \`tool-finalize\` part and no matching tool-result, and throws AI_MissingToolResultsError. The error is mid-stream (after headers flush) so it surfaces via streamText's onError, not the route handler's synchronous catch.

## Acceptance criteria

- Multi-turn chat conversations work — second/third/Nth turn does not throw AI_MissingToolResultsError.
- finalize still halts the agent loop (existing stopWhen behaviour preserved).
- The model still can only end its turn by calling finalize (existing structural empty-output prevention preserved).
- Test exists that exercises a multi-turn message array containing a prior tool-finalize call.

## Affected files

- packages/agent/src/tools/finalize.ts (modify — add execute)
- packages/agent/tests/finalize.test.ts (modify — add execute test)
- packages/agent/tests/agent.test.ts (modify — add multi-turn test)

title: Agent flakes to empty-output on trap_japanese_tea (1/3 rate, navigation tools don't fully prevent)
description:
## Symptom
Run 1 of trap_japanese_tea (RFC 7168, 'What Japanese tea varieties does this protocol define?') produces empty agent output ~1 in 3 runs at temperature 0. Caught observationally during ucs-4il T6 dispatch:

| Run | Result | Score |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | FAIL (empty) | 0.000 |
| 2 | PASS | 1.000 |
| 3 | PASS | 1.000 |

trap_encryption (RFC 2324) does not show the same flake (3/3 pass).

## Why this matters
This is the EXACT failure mode that ucs-3cv (agent hardening sweep) + ucs-tke (navigation tools) were designed to defeat. The `hasToolCall('finalize')` stop condition + strict refusal-with-citation prompt + outline/read_lines tools should make empty output structurally impossible. Yet it still happens ~33% of the time on this specific case.

## Hypothesis
RFC 7168 is longer than RFC 2324 and has many tea-related strings. When asked about 'Japanese tea varieties' (off-topic), the agent's grep loop may match many things (e.g. 'tea' → 20-cap hits) without finding 'Japanese' specifically, burning through the 10-step budget without calling finalize. Stream ends → empty output.

## Fix options
1. **Increase step budget** (10 → 12 or 15). Quick, low-risk. May not fully solve if the agent's tool-use strategy is the actual bottleneck.
2. **Provider-side fallback** in agent-provider.ts: if stream ends without finalize, synthesize a generic refusal. Safest bottom-up guard.
3. **Tighter prompt:** explicit 'You MUST call finalize even if you found nothing. Empty turn is a failure.'
4. **prepareStep callback** to force finalize at step N-1 if not yet called.

(2) is most robust per the Citations API / structured-output literature. (1) is fastest to try.

## Found by
ucs-4il (T6) trap-case eval. T7 verification will run more samples to characterise variance. Decision: ship ucs-tke with known flake + fix in a follow-up, OR block ucs-tke merge until fixed?

title: agent: stopWhen: stepCountIs(5) can exhaust budget on tool calls without producing text
description:
Surfaced by ucs-xom investigation. packages/agent/src/agent.ts:20 sets stopWhen: stepCountIs(5). On tool-heavy questions (specifically the HTCPCP-TEA varieties question from url-grounding test 2), the model burns all 5 steps on grep_doc tool calls without ever emitting a final text answer. Result: empty agent output reaches the client.

a) Raise the step budget (e.g. stepCountIs(8)) — simplest, but doesn't solve the general problem.
b) Constrain via system prompt — instruct the model to budget at least 1 step for the final text answer.
c) Surface 'budget exhausted without text' as a typed error from streamChat — caller decides what to do.
d) Use a different stop condition — e.g. stop when 'text-end' chunk emitted, with grep budget separate from text budget.

title: Orchestrator: .beads/issues.jsonl drift after pr-merge
description:
## Problem
`.beads/issues.jsonl` is git-tracked but written by `bd` as a side-effect of reads/writes. After every `pr-merge`, the recipe stashes the working-tree drift, fast-forwards main, drops the stash, then runs `bd export -o .beads/issues.jsonl --no-memories`. This leaves the file dirty on main with the post-merge state — drift gets included in the next worktree's first commit (the empty `chore: open draft PR` bootstrap), polluting unrelated PRs.

## Symptom (URL-fetcher run, this session)
After each of 10 implementation merges, I had to `git checkout .beads/issues.jsonl` on main to discard the post-merge drift before creating the next worktree. Otherwise the drift propagated as an extra `1 file changed` in the bootstrap commit of the next PR. Every iteration. Manual.

## Impact
Each task in the pipeline carries a meaningless `.beads/issues.jsonl` diff. Adds noise to every PR. Doesn't break anything but obscures real changes during review.

## Suggested fixes (pick one)
1. **Drop `bd export` from `pr-merge`.** Dolt is the source of truth; the jsonl snapshot becomes stale between merges anyway. Add a single periodic chore PR (or daily cron) that refreshes the snapshot.
2. **Commit the post-merge jsonl as a follow-up auto-chore.** After `bd close`, create a tiny chore commit + chore PR + safe-merge in the background.
3. **Stop tracking `.beads/issues.jsonl` in git.** Use `bd dolt push` / `bd dolt pull` (Dolt remote) as the inter-clone sync mechanism. The jsonl becomes purely local-readable.

Probably option 3 long-term; option 1 short-term.

title: Orchestrator: .env doesn't propagate to git worktrees
description:
## Problem
Git worktrees created by the orchestrator's `pr-open` recipe don't inherit `.env` from the main repo. SvelteKit/Vite reads `.env` from each project root (cwd), so the worktree's dev server can't see the user-managed `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`.

## Symptom (URL-fetcher run, this session)
- First `gate:qa` dispatch for ucs-sot stopped immediately: no `.env` anywhere (user hadn't created it yet).
- After the user created `.env` at the main repo root, the second `gate:qa` dispatch ALSO stopped — `.env` was at `/Users/sara/Projects/URL-Cheat-Sheet/.env` but the worktree at `/Users/sara/Projects/wt-ucs-sot/.env` was missing.
- I manually `ln -s /Users/sara/Projects/URL-Cheat-Sheet/.env /Users/sara/Projects/wt-ucs-sot/.env` and the third dispatch worked.

The same problem applies to the eval-runner (also needs `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`).

## Impact
Every UI/eval gate run from a worktree blocks until the human (or orchestrator) symlinks `.env`. Two unnecessary "stopped, asking user" cycles per QA run.

## Suggested fix
In `opening-pr-orchestrator`'s `pr-open` recipe, after `git worktree add ...`, add:
```bash
[ -f "$REPO_ROOT/.env" ] && ln -sf "$REPO_ROOT/.env" "$WT/.env"
```
This is NOT creating or populating `.env` (the project's user-managed rule). It exposes the user's existing file at a logical path. If no `.env` exists, the symlink is skipped — same behavior as today.

Also: document this in `.claude/skills/qa-standard/SKILL.md` so QA agents know to expect/respect the symlink rather than re-asking.

title: Orchestrator: bd ready / bv don't recognize custom 'ready' status
description:
## Problem
The orchestrator pipeline (`/claim-next` slash command, `bv --robot-priority`) is documented to query `bd ready` to pick the next claimable issue. But `bd ready` only counts issues with `status=open`. Custom statuses `enriched` and `ready` (provisioned by `scripts/setup-bd.sh`) are invisible to it, even though they are marked `[active]` in `bd statuses`.

## Symptom (URL-fetcher run, this session)
After `task-enrichment` set 10 issues to `enriched`, `bd ready` returned "No open issues". After explicit `enriched → ready` promotion, `bd ready` still returned empty. `bv --robot-priority` returned `[]`. The orchestrator entrypoint cannot do step 2 of its own recipe without manual workaround (`bd list --status=ready` + handpicking unblocked items).

## Impact
Every orchestrator-driven implementation cycle needs a manual issue-pick step. The whole "claim-next picks top-priority ready issue" automation is broken.

## Suggested fixes (pick one)
1. **Drop custom statuses, use built-in workflow:** `proposed`/`enriched` → `open`. The active-status semantics already exist. Less ceremony.
2. **Teach bd that `ready` is open-equivalent:** look for a `status.ready-includes` config or add one upstream.
3. **Rewrite `/claim-next` to query by label/status explicitly:** `bd list --status=ready --json | jq` for unblocked + highest-priority. No bv dependency.

Pick 3 for fastest patch; consider 1 longer-term if custom statuses don't earn their keep.

title: CI eval-gate broken: wrong bun-filter syntax + invalid promptfoo --output
description:
The CI eval-gate job fails deterministically on any PR that touches `packages/agent/**` or `packages/evals/**`. Surfaced by PR #7 (ucs-n3d, the first agent-touching PR after the eval-gate was wired in).

## Two root causes
1. **Wrong bun-filter argument order in `package.json`.** The root `eval` script is `bun --filter '@url-cheat-sheet/evals' run eval`. On bun 1.3.14 this errors with `error: No packages matched the filter`. The working form is `bun --filter '@url-cheat-sheet/evals' eval` — `run` is rejected between the filter and the script name.
2. **`packages/evals/src/run.ts` passes `--output json` to promptfoo.** `--output` expects a file path, not a format string. promptfoo crashes with `Invariant failed: Unsupported output file format: json. Please use one of: csv, html, json, jsonl, txt, xml, yaml, yml, junit.xml.`

## Fix
- `package.json`: drop `run` from the root `eval` script (matches the working `dev` script pattern).
- `packages/evals/src/run.ts`: write to an explicit `.json` file path (e.g., a temp file or `.promptfoo/last-run.json`), then read it back. Update `spawnSync` args accordingly.

## Blast radius
All five RFC 2324 MVP impl PRs (ucs-n3d, ucs-4g0, ucs-23r touch `packages/agent/**`; ucs-3fa and ucs-s0x don't trigger eval-gate per the paths-filter so they're unaffected). 

## Why I'm filing instead of fixing inline on ucs-n3d
ucs-n3d is scoped to "bundle the RFC". The eval-gate bugs predate it. Mixing the fix into ucs-n3d would muddy the PR and the bd history. Per the orchestrator failure-handling rules, CI-fail-not-caused-by-PR is escalated rather than papered over.

title: [qa-defect] StatusPill text frozen on initial mount value — scrambleIn captures node.textContent and breaks Svelte reactive text updates
description:
## Summary When the `state` prop of `StatusPill` changes (e.g., grep_doc transitioning from `input-streaming` → `output-available`, which should flip the pill from `[ SCANNING ]` to `[ N HITS ]`), the DOM `` inside `.status-pill` does not re-render with the new value. The text remains stuck at whatever was first rendered on mount. ## Repro (live in `feat/ucs-s9c-qa-phase2-closeout` worktree) 1. `bun run --filter @url-cheat-sheet/web dev` 2. Open http://localhost:5173/ in a focused (visible) tab 3. Save Anthropic key in settings drawer 4. Submit URL: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc2324 5. Ask: "What HTTP status codes does this document define?" 6. Wait for full response (~1m). ## Expected (per spec §5.1, §5.2 and unit tests at MessageStream.test.ts:192/312) After the SSE stream completes, pills should read: - OUTLINE → `[ NO_SECTIONS ]` or `[ N SECTIONS ]` - GREP_DOC × 2 → `[ N HITS ]` or `[ NO_HITS ]` - READ_LINES → `[ L–L ]` - FINALIZE → `[ COMPILED ]` ## Observed All five pills remain on their intermediate mount-time value: - OUTLINE → `[ SCANNING ]` (despite `data-state=output-available` and body rendering "no sections") - GREP_DOC × 2 → `[ SCANNING ]` (despite sweep `data-state=done`) - READ_LINES → `[ READING ]` (despite `data-state=output-available` and the snippet text rendered in 
)
- FINALIZE → `[ COMPILING ]` (despite full final answer streamed + citations footer rendered + `chat.status` back to `ready`)

A MutationObserver on the pill  over 30+ seconds during streaming captured **zero** text/childList mutations — Svelte is not updating the text node at all.

## Root cause hypothesis

`StatusPill.svelte` line 38:

```
{state}
```

`scrambleIn` (apps/web/src/lib/motion/scrambleIn.ts) calls `gsap.to(node, { scrambleText: { text: finalText } })` on mount. GSAP's `ScrambleTextPlugin` writes to the node by manipulating its inner content during the scramble, and finalizes by setting `node.textContent = finalText`. That assignment detaches Svelte's tracked text node — subsequent reactive updates of `{state}` write to an orphan node, never the live DOM.

Evidence:
- Unit tests for MessageStream pass (15/15) because gsap.ScrambleTextPlugin is not registered in the JSDOM test env — vitest stderr shows `Invalid property scrambleText set to ... Missing plugin? gsap.registerPlugin()` for every test. The plugin no-ops in test, so Svelte reactivity works, so the test asserts pass. In dev/prod, `registerGsap()` runs on +layout.svelte mount and the plugin IS active — that's when the bug fires.

## Affected files

- apps/web/src/lib/components/chat/StatusPill.svelte (the use:scrambleIn site)
- apps/web/src/lib/motion/scrambleIn.ts (the action that mutates textContent)

## Suggested directions for impl team (not prescriptive)

1. Have scrambleIn target a sibling/child node Svelte doesn't track for the `{state}` interpolation (e.g., scrambleIn writes into a separate  that mirrors state on prop change via a Svelte action update handler).
2. Or: convert scrambleIn into an action that tracks the `state` value reactively (accept `text` as a param, re-fire scramble on text change), and pass `{state}` to it instead of relying on `textContent` capture.
3. Or: write a custom JS-level character-by-character animation that mutates a `style` property or `data-attribute` rather than the live text node, so Svelte's text reactivity is preserved.

## Why this blocks s9c

Spec §5.1 / §5.2 / §5.5 require status pills to reflect terminal tool state for all four shipped tool types. Without that, every chat turn ends with all scan cards looking like they're still in flight, even after the final answer is rendered — direct violation of the cinematic memex HUD spec's instrumentation contract.

## Plan reference

docs/plans/2026-05-20-cinematic-memex-hud.v2.md — Task 14 acceptance criteria (Case 3 specifically); spec docs/specs/2026-05-20-cinematic-memex-hud.md §5.1, §5.2, §5.5.

title: [qa-defect] outline + read_lines tools have no scan vocabulary — 200+ console warnings per chat turn, spec §5.5 violation
description:
## Surface
Case 7 — console errors / warnings. Real chat turn against /api/chat with RFC 2324 loaded.

## Expected (spec §5.5)
Every shipped tool gets a deliberate scan vocabulary. No tool falls back to a 'default' visual — each gets a named interior primitive or is not ready to ship.

## Actual
The agent (packages/agent/src/tools/) ships FOUR tools — finalize, grep_doc, outline, read_lines. MessageStream.svelte (apps/web/src/lib/components/chat/MessageStream.svelte) only registers scans for two — grep_doc and finalize. The other two:

- 'tool-outline' — called on every chat turn (the agent surfaces the document outline early)
- 'tool-read_lines' — called for line-range citations

Each call fires console.warn('[MessageStream] unknown tool type "<type>" — no scan registered') and renders nothing in the assistant message. A single multi-step chat turn produced **210+ console warnings** during a single QA session (Case 7), the bulk of them split between these two tools.

## Reproduction
1. Start dev server with valid ANTHROPIC_API_KEY in .env.
2. Load https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc2324.html.
3. Ask any question that requires multi-step tool use (e.g. 'Compare the security vs safety considerations').
4. Open DevTools Console — count the '[MessageStream] unknown tool type' warnings.

## Severity
Major. Two concerns:
1. Console spam — Case 7's 'no console errors / warnings on any state or transition' acceptance criterion fails. 210 warnings is signal-destroying noise.
2. Functional regression — the user sees parts of the agent's reasoning vanish. The outline call and the read_lines snippets are the system's archival voice (spec §5.4: 'completed scan cards stay visible — they are the visible trace of what the system did') but they paint nothing.

## Fix sketch
Either:
(a) Ship Phase-2 scan vocabulary for outline + read_lines, OR
(b) Reduce the warning to a single dev-mode log and render the existing ScanCard chrome with a neutral 'TOOL: <name>' header until vocabulary lands.

Option (a) is what the spec actually requires; option (b) is the QA-defensible interim if the impl team needs another sprint.

title: [qa-defect] GrepDocScan always shows [ 0 HITS ] — MessageStream.hitsFor reads output.hits but tool returns output.matches
description:
## Surface
Case 3 — tool-call choreography, real chat against /api/chat.

## Expected (spec §5.1)
After a grep_doc scan completes, the status pill scrambles from [ SCANNING ] to '[ <n> HITS ]' (or [ NO_HITS ] if zero), with the hit count phosphor-flashing once. The hit count must reflect the actual number of matches returned by the tool.

## Actual
Every GrepDocScan card pill shows '[ 0 HITS ]' on completion, even when the tool actually returned matches. Verified against the real /api/chat SSE: grep_doc returned output.matches = [{line: 1, text: '...'}] (one real match), but the card shows 0 HITS.

## Root cause
- apps/web/src/lib/components/chat/MessageStream.svelte#hitsFor(output) reads output.hits (array length) or output.count.
- packages/agent/src/tools/grep-doc.ts returns { matches: GrepMatch[] }.
- Field name mismatch: hitsFor returns null because output.hits is undefined; GrepDocScan then renders 'done' state with hits ?? 0 → '0 HITS'.

## Reproduction
Same as ucs-aoo (sibling defect): load RFC 2324, ask about HTTP status codes. Confirm via /api/chat SSE that output.matches has length ≥ 1 while the pill shows 0 HITS.

## Severity
Major. The hit count is the second load-bearing piece of grep_doc UI vocabulary (after the query) — without it the user has no idea whether the system found anything. Same fix touch point as ucs-aoo.

## Fix sketch
Rename hitsFor to read output.matches.length (or alias the tool output). Consider promoting the tool input/output shapes from packages/schemas/src/tools.ts to a single source of truth so MessageStream and the tool schema can't drift again.

title: [qa-defect] GrepDocScan shows empty q:"" — MessageStream.queryFor reads input.query but tool schema uses input.pattern
description:
## Surface
Case 3 — tool-call choreography, all viewports, real chat against /api/chat.

## Expected (spec §5.1)
The grep_doc scan card renders the query string after a 'q:' prefix in body sans, scrambling in on first paint. The query should reflect the actual search term the model issued.

## Actual
Every GrepDocScan card renders 'q: ""' (empty query) regardless of what the model called grep_doc with. Verified against the real /api/chat SSE: the model issued grep_doc({pattern: '2.3'}) but the card shows q: "".

## Root cause
- apps/web/src/lib/components/chat/MessageStream.svelte#queryFor(input) reads input.query.
- packages/agent/src/tools/grep-doc.ts tool schema declares input as { pattern: z.union([string, array]) }.
- Field name mismatch: queryFor returns '' because input.query is undefined.

## Reproduction
1. Start dev server with valid ANTHROPIC_API_KEY in .env.
2. Load https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc2324.html via the URL form.
3. Once in ready state, ask 'What HTTP status codes does this document define?'
4. Observe grep_doc scan cards in the assistant message — query line shows q: "" instead of the actual pattern.

## Severity
Major. The card chrome and animation are functional, but the visible query is the load-bearing identifier of what the model searched — the spec's whole 'visible trace of system reasoning' (§5.4) is broken for grep_doc.

## Fix sketch
Either rename the tool prop in MessageStream.queryFor to read input.pattern (joining arrays for the array form), or alias the tool input field. The hits readout (output.matches vs output.hits) is the same shape mismatch — see sibling defect.

title: Evals harness: promptfoo subprocess cwd doesn't load repo-root .env
description:
## Symptom
url-grounding eval smoke runs silently produce 0-token empty-output failures on all cases when ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is only present at repo-root .env (not exported in the parent shell). Discovered during ucs-ec6 (T5) smoke run.

## Cause
`packages/evals/src/run.ts` spawns `bunx promptfoo eval ...` with `cwd: packageRoot` (i.e. `packages/evals/`). Bun only auto-loads .env from cwd. The user-managed .env lives at repo root; worktree symlinks it at the worktree root (per opening-pr-orchestrator skill). Neither location is the packageRoot promptfoo sees.

## Workaround
Export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY in the shell before invoking the suite. Or symlink .env from repo root into packages/evals/.

## Fix options
- run.ts could load repo-root .env explicitly and pass through env vars to the spawned subprocess (cleanest)
- Add a packages/evals/.env symlink in the bootstrap recipe (mechanical, may surprise users)
- Document in packages/evals/README.md as the required env setup (minimum)

title: Motion actions — scanSweep + assembleCascade (tool-call interiors)
description:
## Acceptance criteria
- `scanSweep` action signature: `(node, { trigger, duration? })`. Animates a child scanline element via `gsap.to` from `top: 0%` to `top: 100%` with opacity timeline `0 → 0.9 → 0.4` peaking mid-traversal. Default duration 600ms, `--ease-out-expo`.
- `assembleCascade` action signature: `(node, { streamedChars, totalEstimatedChars })`. On every `update`, animates a child `.compile-bar` element's height to `(streamedChars / totalEstimatedChars)` capped at 100%. New text lines (detected via prop diff or MutationObserver on text container) scramble-in (~180ms per line).
- Both actions honor `prefers-reduced-motion` per ADR 0009: scanline skipped, compile bar jumps to current %, text appears without scramble.
- `GrepDocScan`: scanline child + `use:scanSweep` triggered by state transitions into `'scanning'`. On completion (`state === 'done' | 'no-hits'`): glyph-grid backdrop dims to 4% opacity. `finalize` is a client-side sentinel — render `part.input.answer`, not `part.output`.
- `FinalizeScan`: `.compile-bar` left-edge child + `use:assembleCascade` driven by `(input.answer ?? '').length` and a locally-tracked totalEstimatedChars (running max + 200 buffer heuristic). On `output-available`: `phosphorFlash` the compile bar once.
- Failure / cancellation per spec §5.3: `[ FAULTED ]` in `--amber-alarm` freezes mid-motion, dims to 30%, shows `!` glyph (no phosphor flash on failures); `[ HALTED ]` in `--bone-dim` leaves bar at last position.
- vitest tests with `vi.mock('gsap')` for each action.

title: writing-plans: code blocks not compile-checked against installed deps
description:
## Problem
Plans written by `superpowers:writing-plans` include verbatim code blocks. Implementation agents are told to follow them literally. But the code blocks aren't compile-checked / smoke-tested against installed deps — several were wrong in the URL-fetcher v2 plan in non-obvious ways.

## Symptom (URL-fetcher run, this session)
At least 4 plan code blocks needed agent-side reconciliation:
1. **ucs-1fd** — `chatRequestSchema` was prescribed as required-`document` from Task 1, but pre-existing chat-route tests don't send `document`. Made optional in Task 1, tightened in Task 8. (Caught at first impl, plan defect.)
2. **ucs-84u** — vard adapter sketch used `result.threats` directly; vard's actual API is a discriminated union with `{ safe, threats? }`. Wrong field name (`category` vs `type`), wrong enum members (`encodingAttacks`/`obfuscation` don't exist). Agent reconciled against `node_modules/@andersmyrmel/vard/dist/index.d.ts`.
3. **ucs-kk6** — `sample-article.html` fixture's title-extraction test failed because Readability's `_getArticleTitle()` heuristics didn't match the plan's verbatim fixture (em-dash separator, two H1s). Agent retuned the fixture.
4. **ucs-mgr** — `FETCH_DEFAULTS.allowedSchemes.has(target.protocol)` failed under TS strict because `as const` narrows `Set` to literal-type members. Required `as ReadonlySet<string>` casts.

Each one cost an extra fix-pass or careful agent judgment.

## Impact
Plan defects amplify across the chain. Every wrong code block burns 1-2 review passes. The plan-review (`improving-plans`) pass catches some, but not deps-compile-state issues.

## Suggested fixes
1. **Compile-check code blocks before writing the plan.** Drop them into a scratch package, run `tsc --noEmit` against the installed dep versions. Issues like #4 above would surface immediately.
2. **Verify API surfaces against installed type defs.** When the plan calls `library.method(args)`, the writing-plans skill should grep the lib's `.d.ts` and confirm the method/args exist as written. Vard would have caught issue #2.
3. **Prefer interfaces + constraints over full code.** Have the plan specify the function signature + acceptance criteria + edge cases, but let the impl agent write the body against actual installed deps. Reduces the surface area for plan-vs-reality drift.

Option 3 has the best long-term cost-benefit ratio.

title: safeFetch TLS handshake fails for HTTPS under Node (vite dev / prod)
description:
## Symptom
POST /api/extract with any HTTPS URL returns 504 `{kind: FETCH_NETWORK}` under the SvelteKit dev server (`vite dev`, which runs under Node even when launched via `bun run`). Confirmed reproducibly against:
- https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc2324.html → 504 FETCH_NETWORK
- https://example.com/this-is-not-a-real-path → 504 FETCH_NETWORK
- http://example.com/ (redirects to https) → 502 FETCH_HTTP_ERROR

## Root cause
`packages/agent/src/url/fetch.ts` rewrites the URL hostname to the pinned IP and passes the original hostname via the `host` header. Bun's fetch handles SNI correctly in this shape, but Node's undici-based fetch sends SNI based on the URL hostname (now an IP), causing the TLS server (Cloudflare, etc.) to abort the handshake:

```
TypeError: fetch failed
cause: ssl3_read_bytes:ssl/tls alert handshake failure: SSL alert number 40
```

Standalone Bun execution of `safeFetch` works (verified by running the same code via `bun run`). The bug is platform-specific to Node-based runtimes (vite dev, Vercel serverless functions if not Bun adapter).

## Impact
- gate:qa for ucs-sot blocked — happy-path, change-URL, flagged, and error-404 scenarios all fail at the extract step (only "Blocked URL" passes since it short-circuits before fetch).
- If prod uses any non-Bun runtime, every HTTPS URL fetch is broken.

## Suggested fixes (pick one)
1. Use undici `Agent` with `connect.servername` set to the original hostname (Node-only path).
2. Skip IP pinning post-validation — keep SSRF guard via pre-fetch DNS check but let fetch redo the lookup. Lose TOCTOU resistance.
3. Branch on runtime: keep current behavior under Bun, use SNI-aware path under Node.

## Error-handling miss (secondary)
`apps/web/src/routes/api/extract/+server.ts` returns `message: kind` instead of the real error string (`String(e)` already captured by safeFetch), making the failure invisible to the client. Worth fixing alongside.

## Repro
1. `cd /Users/sara/Projects/wt-ucs-sot && bun run --filter @url-cheat-sheet/web dev`
2. `curl -X POST http://localhost:5173/api/extract -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"url":"https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc2324.html"}'`
3. Observe `{"kind":"FETCH_NETWORK","message":"FETCH_NETWORK"}` 504.

title: opening-pr-orchestrator pr-merge: 'gh pr checks --required' is empty, preflight aborts
description:
## Problem
The `pr-merge` preflight in `.claude/skills/opening-pr-orchestrator/SKILL.md` does:

```bash
CHECKS=\"\$(gh pr checks \"\$PR_URL\" --required --json state -q '.[].state')\"
[ -z \"\$CHECKS\" ] && { echo \"abort: no required checks reported (branch protection misconfigured?)\"; exit 1; }
```

But this repo (per ADR 0005) intentionally does NOT configure GitHub branch protection required checks — it uses a local pre-push hook instead. So `gh pr checks --required` returns empty, and the preflight aborts every merge.

Workaround I used: read `statusCheckRollup` directly:

```bash
ROLLUP=\"\$(gh pr view \"\$PR_URL\" --json statusCheckRollup | jq -r '.statusCheckRollup[] | .conclusion')\"
echo \"\$ROLLUP\" | grep -qvE '^(SUCCESS|SKIPPED)\$' && { echo 'abort: CI not green'; exit 1; }
```

## Fix options
1. Replace the `--required` check with the rollup check above. Simpler, works for this repo.
2. Configure GitHub branch protection with required checks. Reopens ADR 0005's decision; the user previously chose local hook over GH protection. Worth revisiting in light of ucs-0z5 (auto-merge fires on red CI — would also be solved by required checks).
3. Both: rollup-based preflight now, branch protection later as a defense-in-depth.

Related: ucs-0z5 (auto-merge on red CI). Same root cause; same potential fix path.

title: opening-pr-orchestrator pr-open: branch with no commits ahead rejects PR creation
description:
## Problem
The `pr-open` recipe in `.claude/skills/opening-pr-orchestrator/SKILL.md` does:

```bash
git push -u origin "feat/$ID-$SLUG"
gh pr create --draft --base main --head "feat/$ID-$SLUG" ...
```

But a freshly-created worktree branch is identical to `main`. `gh pr create` errors: `pull request create failed: GraphQL: No commits between main and feat/...`.

## Reproduce
Every RFC 2324 MVP impl PR (ucs-n3d, ucs-4g0, ucs-23r, ucs-3fa, ucs-s0x) hit this. Workaround was a `git commit --allow-empty -m "chore(<id>): open draft PR for orchestrator tracking"` before the push.

## Fix options
1. **Empty commit before push** — bake `git commit --allow-empty -m "chore($ID): open draft PR for orchestrator tracking"` into the recipe between branch creation and `git push`. Simple, mirrors what I did manually.
2. **Skip pr-open entirely until first real commit** — move PR creation to first push of impl content. Means the issue spends part of its life with no PR URL. Bad for tracking.

Option 1 is the right tradeoff.

- `.claude/skills/opening-pr-orchestrator/SKILL.md` (the recipe text)
- `docs/specs/2026-05-18-agentic-pr-loop.md` (§4.1)

title: Orchestrator merges PRs with failing CI (no GH required checks)
description:
ADR 0005 routes branch protection through a local pre-push hook (`scripts/git-hooks/pre-push`) rather than GitHub branch protection. The pre-push hook only stops direct pushes to `main`; it does NOT keep `gh pr merge --auto` from firing when a PR's CI is red. PR #8 demonstrated this: its `lint` job failed (prettier flagged `packages/evals/src/run.ts`), but the auto-merge queue merged it anyway when the PR became "mergeable" in GitHub's eyes.

Surfaced consequence: the next PR pulling main (PR #7, ucs-n3d after rebase) inherited the prettier failure and had to absorb a cleanup commit it shouldn't have owned.

## Possible fixes
1. Configure required status checks in branch protection — re-opens the question ADR 0005 closed. Worth revisiting now that we know the cost of the alternative.
2. Replace `gh pr merge --auto --squash` in `opening-pr-orchestrator` with a polling step that asserts CI green before issuing the merge. Doable, but pushes the check into orchestrator code and skips for non-orchestrator merges.
3. Both: a script-level guard now (option 2) plus the right branch-protection config later (option 1).

## How to reproduce
1. Create a PR whose lint job fails (e.g., introduce unformatted code).
2. `gh pr merge <num> --auto --squash`.
3. Watch CI complete with lint=FAILURE.
4. PR merges anyway.

title: HudPanel alarm variant: corner brackets don't tint at runtime
description:
## Surface
PR #87 (ucs-wny) gate:review caught:

`apps/web/src/lib/components/hud/HudPanel.svelte:90` — `.hud-panel--alarm .hud-panel__corner { border-color: var(--amber-alarm); }` is *overridden* by the later `.hud-panel__corner--{tl,tr,bl,br}` rules that set `border-top/right/bottom/left: 1px solid var(--hair)` individually. CSS shorthand cascade resolves the per-edge shorthands as winning, so the alarm variant tints only the panel itself, not the four L-shaped corner brackets.

## Why this missed
Not in the acceptance criteria — criterion was "variant='alarm' retints border", which the panel border does. Reviewer flagged as cosmetic polish.

## Impact
Visible in extract-error state (Task 4) — the corner brackets stay bone-colored while the panel border goes amber. Slight visual disconnect.

## Fix options
1. Reorder CSS so `.hud-panel--alarm .hud-panel__corner { border-color: var(--amber-alarm); }` comes AFTER the per-corner border declarations.
2. Use `:where()` to lower specificity on the per-corner rules.
3. Apply alarm tint via a CSS custom property on the bracket spans (cleaner long-term).

## Acceptance
- Alarm variant tints all four corner brackets to `--amber-alarm` at runtime.
- New visual test or existing HudPanel test extended to assert computed border-color on a corner span under alarm variant.

## Defer until
Task 4 (ucs-9g9 — extract-error + flagged states) is the first consumer that actually exercises alarm. Bundle the fix with that task or close separately before Task 4 lands.
close_reason: Fixed in ucs-9g9 via PR (alarm variant now tints corner brackets at runtime; new test added)

title: impl subagents re-discover workspace conventions per dispatch
description:
## Problem
Every impl subagent gets a fresh context and needs to be re-briefed on workspace conventions: TS-strict, `verbatimModuleSyntax`, Zod 4 idioms, "chatRequestSchema stays z.object", "ANTHROPIC_API_KEY check preserved in /api/chat", "preserve `as UIMessage[]` cast", "no undici/http.Agent SSRF libs (Bun footgun)", etc.

These live in CLAUDE.md (project + global) but agents don't always weight them appropriately when implementing.

## Symptom (URL-fetcher run, this session)
- ucs-1fd's first dispatch made `chatRequestSchema` strict despite CLAUDE.md's existing pattern; caught by review and the v1→v2 plan review.
- Multiple agents needed the SSRF footgun pointed out explicitly in their prompt.
- ucs-mgr's impl agent didn't anticipate the Bun-vs-Node SNI difference; caught by gate:qa as ucs-u47.

My agent prompts had to enumerate "things to know" each time. Each enumeration takes prompt-writing effort and could miss a key constraint.

## Suggested fixes
1. **Per-team "must-read" files.** `.claude/teams/agent-impl-team.md` already lists "owned paths" and "skills." Add a "must-read constraints" section that maps to specific paragraphs in CLAUDE.md, the spec, the relevant ADRs. Orchestrator includes those in every impl dispatch.
2. **Pre-commit hooks for the obvious mechanical rules** (`z.object` vs `strictObject` for AI-SDK-touching schemas, etc.). Lint-style enforcement that catches the rule violations the impl agent missed.
3. **The orchestrator could prepend a "common constraints" block** to every impl-team dispatch, parameterized by team. Reduces per-task prompt-writing burden.

Probably option 1 + 3 in combination.

title: pr-merge preflight false-aborts on IN_PROGRESS CI checks
description:
## Problem
`pr-merge` preflight in `opening-pr-orchestrator` runs:
```bash
ROLLUP="$(gh pr view "$PR_URL" --json statusCheckRollup -q '.statusCheckRollup[] | .conclusion')"
[ -z "$ROLLUP" ] && { echo "abort: no CI checks reported"; exit 1; }
echo "$ROLLUP" | grep -qvE '^(SUCCESS|SKIPPED)$' && { echo "abort: CI not green"; exit 1; }
```

When a check is `IN_PROGRESS`, `conclusion` is an empty string (status, not conclusion). The `grep -qvE` matches the empty line as not-`SUCCESS|SKIPPED` and aborts spuriously.

## Symptom (URL-fetcher run, this session)
ucs-drn's pr-merge aborted with "abort: CI not green" while a freshly-triggered eval-gate run was IN_PROGRESS even though all other checks had passed. Required manual re-run after CI fully settled.

## Impact
False aborts during the normal merge flow. Especially common when GitHub re-triggers CI on PR comment / label changes (which the gate:review clear does).

## Suggested fix
Distinguish three states in the preflight:
- **No checks reported** → abort (PR isn't ready)
- **Any check IN_PROGRESS / QUEUED** → wait (or abort with "wait for CI", not "CI not green")
- **Any check FAILURE / CANCELLED / TIMED_OUT** → abort "CI failed"
- **All SUCCESS or SKIPPED** → proceed

Use `--json statusCheckRollup -q '.statusCheckRollup[] | {name, status, conclusion}'` and branch on `status === 'COMPLETED'` first.

title: bd worktree permission warning noise (0755 vs 0700)
description:
## Problem
Every `bd` invocation in a git worktree prints:
```
Warning: /Users/sara/Projects/wt-XXX/.beads has permissions 0755 (recommended: 0700). Run: chmod 700 /Users/sara/Projects/wt-XXX/.beads
```

Git creates worktrees with 0755 by default. bd wants 0700.

## Symptom (URL-fetcher run, this session)
The warning fired 50+ times across 11 PR cycles — every `bd update`, `bd show`, `bd close`, `bd dep add` from inside a worktree.

## Impact
Pure log noise. Not blocking. Obscures real bd output. Easy to miss actual errors.

## Suggested fixes (pick one)
1. **`chmod 700 .beads/` in the `pr-open` recipe** right after `git worktree add`. One-line addition.
2. **Add an `BEADS_QUIET_PERMS=1` env var** (upstream bd change, or wrapped via project config). Suppress the warning without changing perms.

Option 1 is fastest; do it locally.

title: opening-pr-orchestrator pr-merge: deletes branch held by worktree, fails noisily
description:
## Problem
The `pr-merge` recipe runs:
```bash
cd \"\$(git rev-parse --git-common-dir)/..\"   # main repo root
gh pr merge \"\$PR_URL\" --squash --delete-branch
...
git worktree remove \"../wt-\$ID\"
```

`gh pr merge --delete-branch` tries to delete the LOCAL branch too (after the remote merge), but the local branch is still checked out in `../wt-\$ID`. Result every time:
```
failed to delete local branch feat/...: error: cannot delete branch '...' used by worktree at '/Users/sara/Projects/wt-...'
```

The merge itself works (remote is deleted, PR is closed), but the error message is noisy and the local branch sticks around until `git worktree remove ../wt-\$ID` and then `git branch -D ...`.

## Fix
Reorder the recipe:
```bash
git worktree remove \"../wt-\$ID\" --force      # before gh merge --delete-branch
gh pr merge \"\$PR_URL\" --squash --delete-branch
```

Or drop `--delete-branch` from gh and do `git push origin --delete feat/...` after worktree removal — cleaner.

Either way, the worktree must be removed BEFORE the local branch is deleted. Current recipe does it after.

title: opening-pr-orchestrator pr-ready: GNU 'date -Is' is non-portable
description:
## Problem
The `pr-ready` recipe in `.claude/skills/opening-pr-orchestrator/SKILL.md` records the review-pass timestamp via:

```bash
bd update "$ID" --append-note "review-pass:$N — submitted by impl-team @ \$(date -Is)"
```

macOS BSD `date` rejects `-Is` (it's a GNU extension). Result on macOS: `date: invalid argument 's' for -I`, and the bd note ends with a blank timestamp.

## Repro
On macOS:
```
$ date -Is
date: invalid argument 's' for -I
```

## Fix
Replace `\$(date -Is)` with `\$(date -u +%FT%TZ)` — portable across GNU and BSD, prints ISO 8601 UTC.

## Files
- `.claude/skills/opening-pr-orchestrator/SKILL.md` (one line in pr-ready)

title: [debt] --ease-out-expo duplicated as JS literal in motion actions
description:
## Surface
PR #112 (ucs-3t6) gate:review flagged: `apps/web/src/lib/motion/splitLineReveal.ts:64` uses the literal `'cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)'` because GSAP can't parse CSS `var(--ease-out-expo)`. This duplicates `tokens.css:47`'s `--ease-out-expo` definition.

## Risk
If `tokens.css` is updated, the JS literal drifts silently. Tasks 10/11/12/13 will compound this (each new motion action that uses the curve will inline the literal).

## Fix options
1. **Read the token at runtime once at module load.** `getComputedStyle(document.documentElement).getPropertyValue('--ease-out-expo')` cached.
2. **Tiny guard test that imports both values and asserts equality.** Cheap, doesn't add runtime cost.
3. **Centralize the JS-side curve constants in a shared module** (`apps/web/src/lib/motion/_curves.ts`) imported by every action. Pair with a tokens.test.ts assertion that the CSS values match. Trades runtime cost for test-time validation.

## Defer
P4. Pick up before Phase 2 ships if convenient, otherwise after.
